title: Google and Singapore Prepare On-Device Scam Detection
summary: Google DeepMind and Singapore’s GovTech have fine-tuned an on-device Gemma system for localized scam conversations; application rollout will be phased and require user consent.
body:
## A local defense against social engineering

Google DeepMind and Singapore’s Government Technology Agency have collaborated on a privacy-preserving, on-device AI model designed to detect scam conversations before users transfer money or reveal credentials. The model has been fine-tuned on local scam conversations involving impersonation of public institutions, banks and local figures. Its rollout within applications will be phased and developed with the Singapore Government, rather than treated as a completed nationwide deployment.

When integrated into an application, the model will process conversation data directly on the device and can trigger a real-time warning when it detects manipulative patterns. The system is intended to identify tactics such as impersonation and other localized social-engineering schemes.

## Why the architecture matters

The model is designed to operate on-device rather than rely on continuous server-side inspection. That is important in encrypted messaging environments, where platforms may not be able to read conversations in the cloud. Processing locally can also reduce response time and limit the amount of sensitive material leaving the device.

Google DeepMind says that, once deployed, the model will access on-device conversations only with the user’s consent and under the application’s terms of use. Because it runs entirely on-device, neither Google nor the Singapore Government will be able to access users’ conversations through the deployment. The partners frame the project as a collaboration between government and model developers to improve protection against Singapore-specific scam patterns.

## Why it matters

This is more than another fraud classifier: it tests whether small, specialized models can become a practical safety layer inside consumer devices. The unresolved questions are false positives, battery use, language coverage, adoption by applications and who controls future updates. If those issues are solved, on-device models could let messaging services add protection without weakening end-to-end privacy.
title_zh: 谷歌与新加坡准备将端侧诈骗识别模型用于应用
summary_zh: 谷歌DeepMind与新加坡GovTech已完成面向本地诈骗对话的端侧Gemma模型微调，后续将在获得用户同意的前提下分阶段集成到应用中。
body_zh:
## 把反诈骗能力放进手机

谷歌DeepMind与新加坡政府科技局合作开发了一套注重隐私保护的端侧人工智能模型，用于在用户转账或泄露凭据前识别诈骗对话。模型已经使用本地诈骗对话完成微调，覆盖冒充公共机构、银行和本地人物等情形。该模型将在应用中分阶段推出，并与新加坡政府共同开发，目前不能表述为已经完成全国范围部署。

当模型被集成到应用后，它会直接在设备上分析对话数据；如果发现操纵性话术，就可以在手机上实时触发警告。系统的目标是识别冒充身份及其他具有本地特征的社会工程诈骗手法。

## 为什么端侧架构值得关注

模型面向设备本地运行，不依赖持续的云端扫描。在端到端加密消息环境中，平台往往无法在服务器侧读取聊天内容；端侧分析既能缩短响应时间，也能减少敏感数据离开设备的机会。

谷歌DeepMind表示，模型部署后只有在用户同意、并符合应用使用条款的情况下，才会访问设备上的对话。由于模型完全在端侧运行，谷歌和新加坡政府都无法通过该部署访问用户聊天内容。双方将该项目定位为政府与模型开发者合作，应对新加坡本地诈骗模式的尝试。

## 为什么重要

这不只是一个新的诈骗分类器，而是在验证小型专用模型能否成为消费设备内置的安全层。它仍面临误报、电量消耗、语言覆盖、应用接入以及更新权归属等问题。若这些限制能够解决，端侧模型有望在不削弱端到端隐私的前提下，为即时通信增加一层防护。

sources.title: On-Device AI Against Scams: Google DeepMind & MDDI
Google DeepMind and Singapore Government announce new AI tool to protect citizens against scams

featured_reason: It is the edition’s clearest example of AI moving from cloud experimentation into privacy-preserving public infrastructure.
featured_reason_zh: 它最清楚地展示了人工智能如何从云端实验走向兼顾隐私的公共基础设施。
cat_take_zh: 端侧Gemma的价值不在模型名气，而在新加坡把隐私约束变成了产品前提。
cat_take_en: The important move is Singapore making privacy a deployment requirement, not a promise added after the model works.
